info.description: Loopback HTTP interface for reading and authoring the open Tableau Desktop document. Clients authenticate with the bearer token published in the per-user discovery file.

post.description: Opens a local file by path. A .twb/.twbx opens as a workbook; a datasource file (Excel, text, spatial, extract, .tds, and the like) attaches to the open workbook, creating one if none is open. An extension Tableau cannot open is rejected before dispatch. Note: opening a workbook when one is already open launches it in a NEW Desktop window, and this API session stays bound to the workbook it started with -- GET /v0/workbook continues to report the original, not the newly opened one.

Note: opening a workbook when one is already open launches it in a NEW Desktop window, and this API session stays bound to the workbook it started with -- GET /v0/workbook continues to report the original, not the newly opened one.

post.description: Refreshes the live data for the datasource resolved by {id} (its internal name from GET /v0/workbook/datasources) the way the toolbar Refresh Data Source does: it lowers the query-cache timestamp and clears the mapped-image cache, then re-fetches the datasource from its source. This is NOT an extract refresh -- if the datasource is backed by an extract, the data stays fresh only through the extract's metadata date. A datasource with no data connection to refresh is a no-op SUCCEEDED Operation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The resource's stable id as returned in its list or GET response, not its display name or caption.

A datasource with no data connection to refresh is a no-op SUCCEEDED Operation.

post.description: Kicks off an extract refresh on the datasource resolved by {id} (its internal name from GET /v0/workbook/datasources). By default the refresh is incremental when the extract supports it; send isFullRefresh=true to force a full refresh. A datasource that has no refreshable extract is a no-op SUCCEEDED Operation.

post.description: Replaces a single dashboard with the submitted Tableau XML, leaving the workbook's other sheets intact. A missing or empty body is rejected with 400 and a non-XML Content-Type with 415. A non-empty XML body that is not well-formed, or that the product cannot load into a valid workbook, is rejected with 422. The payload is NOT validated against the schema; use POST /v0/workbook/document:validate for XSD validation. This apply is unconditional last-writer-wins: it performs no precondition/If-Match check and will overwrite a concurrent edit to the same sheet. The apply is rejected with 409 when the submitted payload's sheet name does not match the target sheet's current name -- for example, if you renamed the sheet in the payload, or another editor renamed it after you read the document -- or when the name-matching payload element is the wrong sheet subtype (a story, <dashboard type='storyboard'>, where the target is a dashboard). A client error returns a Problem Details response with code operation-failed carrying the underlying tableauErrorCode. The 4xx rejection applies when the apply completes synchronously; an apply that returns 202 instead reports the same failure through the polled operation (HTTP 200 with state FAILED and the error).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The resource's stable id as returned in its list or GET response, not its display name or caption.

parameters.name: X-Tableau-Effective-Payload-Version
parameters.description: Reserved for future Tableau payload (file-format) version negotiation. Currently accepted but ignored: documents are always served and applied at the running product version.

requestBody.description: The dashboard's Tableau XML -- either the bare <dashboard> element returned by GET .../dashboards/{id}/document, or that element inside a <workbook> envelope. Only the dashboard whose name matches the target sheet's name is applied, and any other sheets in the payload are ignored. Top-level <datasources> definitions in the payload are ignored, but the applied dashboard's datasource references must still resolve to a datasource already present in the open workbook -- a reference to an absent datasource is rejected with 409.

get.description: Renders a single dashboard (resolved by id) as an image, returned inline as base64 or written to a caller-supplied file path. The id must resolve to a dashboard: an id that matches no sheet returns 404, and an id that resolves to a non-dashboard sheet or to a dashboard that is not yet renderable returns 409.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The resource's stable id as returned in its list or GET response, not its display name or caption.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Path to write the image to. Must be absolute and name a file; a directory, a trailing slash, or any '.'/'..' path segment is rejected with a 400. When set, the response projects this path instead of inline base64; when omitted, the image is returned as base64.

parameters.name: mimeType
parameters.description: Requested image MIME type (e.g. image/png, image/jpeg). The effective type is returned in the response.

post.description: Replaces the open workbook with the submitted Tableau XML. A missing or empty body is rejected with 400 and a non-XML Content-Type with 415. A non-empty XML body that is not well-formed, or that the product cannot load into a valid workbook, is rejected with 422 (a Problem Details response with code operation-failed carrying the underlying tableauErrorCode). The payload is NOT validated against the schema; use POST /v0/workbook/document:validate for XSD validation. This apply is unconditional last-writer-wins: it performs no precondition/If-Match check; it overwrites concurrent edits and (Overwrite policy) deletes sheets the payload omits. A payload that would leave the workbook with no sheets is rejected as a failed operation (HTTP 200 with state FAILED and an error). post.description: Exports the open workbook to a non-native format, leaving the open document unchanged. Both filePath and format are required. format selects what to produce: "pdf" (a PDF of every sheet), "powerpoint" (a .pptx with one slide per sheet), "packaged-workbook" (a .twbx bundling the workbook and its data), or "prior-version" (a down-saved copy for an older Tableau release). filePath must end in the extension that format produces (.pdf, .pptx, .twbx, or .twb/.twbx respectively) or the request is rejected. For "prior-version", also supply targetVersion as the customer-facing release string (e.g. "2024.1"); an unrecognized version is rejected. The export always writes to the supplied filePath and never opens a dialog, so it is fully headless.

post.description: Saves the open workbook. Supply a filePath to save a copy to that path, or omit it to save the workbook in place at the path it already has. filePath must end in .twb or .twbx: save writes workbook content verbatim without converting, so any other extension is rejected rather than writing a mislabeled file. The save is headless whenever the workbook has a writable path to save to -- a supplied filePath, or the existing path of an already-saved workbook whose file can be written. It cannot be headless when there is no writable existing path and no filePath is supplied: a workbook that has never been saved, a workbook whose existing file is read-only, or a workbook recovered from an autosave draft. In those cases the product opens its native Save As dialog, which blocks until a person responds. Supply filePath to keep the save headless.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details. Structured extension members, such as tableauErrorCode, may appear as additional top-level fields.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error identity clients branch on.

Operation.description: The state of a dispatched operation.

WindowInfo.description: A visible modal Qt top-level window observed at read time. Whether a client must act on it is conveyed by which array carries it: blockingWindows for a window that needs a human decision, progressWindows for a self-clearing one. The content fields (messageText, informativeText, detailedText, iconLevel, buttons) are best-effort: QMessageBox exposes them precisely, while generic dialogs scrape visible QLabel/QAbstractButton children and may include incidental labels alongside diagnostic text.

index.description: The sheet's workbook-wide tab position, or null when the sheet is hidden.

WorkbookInventory.description: Metadata and sheet inventory of the open workbook.

WorkbookOptimizerResult.description: Evaluated Workbook Optimizer suggestions for the open workbook.

WorkbookOptimizerSuggestion.description: The evaluated outcome of one optimizer rule.

WorkbookOptimizerAffected.description: Structured workbook objects affected by an optimizer rule.

WorkbookOptimizerAffectedItem.description: A named affected object with an optional value or children.

OperationList.description: Async operations. List entries omit each operation's `result` and per-operation `blockingWindows`: fetch GET /v0/operations/{id} for an operation's `result`, and read blocking-window state once from the top-level `blockingWindows` here.

DatasourceItem.description: A datasource used by the open workbook.

type.description: The datasource's backend kind, independent of whether it is an extract (see isExtract).

isExtract.description: True if the datasource is currently backed by an extract rather than a live connection.

hasDownloadFilePermission.description: Whether the current user has server permission to download the published datasource file (the Download/Save a Copy permission). Not whether the data can be queried or extracted. null for a datasource that is not published, where the permission does not apply.

SiteWorkbookItem.description: A workbook published to the connected site.

SiteDatasourceItem.description: A datasource published to the connected site.

ImageExport.description: The result of exporting a sheet as an image.

SummaryData.description: Tabular worksheet data as columns and rows. Returned by both the summary-data and underlying-data endpoints; the shape is identical for each.

LogicalTableItem.description: A logical table available for a worksheet's data.

ValidationResult.description: The outcome of validating a workbook document.

ShowMeRequest.description: The Show Me visualization to apply to a worksheet.

showMeType.description: The serialized Show Me visualization type to apply.

dataSource.description: Optional internal datasource name used to resolve selected fields.

fieldsSelectedInSchemaViewer.description: Optional fully qualified encoded field names, each with at least a datasource and field component. An explicit empty array supplies an empty field selection; omission preserves ambient selection.

SortRequest.description: The sort to apply to a field on the worksheet.

fieldName.description: The on-shelf field to sort, given as its field-instance name qualified by its datasource caption, in the form [Datasource Caption].[field-instance] (e.g. "[Sample - Superstore].[none:Ship Mode:nk]"). The base column name (e.g. "[Sample - Superstore].[Ship Mode]") will not match any field on the view and the sort is silently ignored.

direction.description: Sort direction; defaults to 'asc' when omitted. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

sortType.description: Sort type; defaults to 'data-source-order' when omitted. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

clearSort.description: When true, removes the existing sort on `fieldName` instead of applying one; `fieldName` is still required.

filePath.description: Path to save a copy to; must end in .twb or .twbx. Omit to save the workbook in place at its current path.

ExportAsWorkbookRequest.description: What to export and where to write it.

filePath.description: Path to write the export to. Must be absolute and name a file; a directory, a trailing slash, or any '.'/'..' path segment is rejected with a 400. Its extension must match format: .pdf for pdf, .pptx for powerpoint, .twbx for packaged-workbook, and .twb or .twbx for prior-version.

format.description: The export format that selects what file to produce. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

targetVersion.description: Required when format is prior-version: the customer-facing Tableau release to down-save to (e.g. "2024.1"). Ignored for other formats.

isFullRefresh.description: Force a full refresh instead of an incremental one. Defaults to false: incremental when the extract supports it, otherwise a full refresh.

ApiRoot.description: API versions and the resource link map.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed. The code field identifies the specific problem, such as a missing required header or an unreadable body.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer token was missing or invalid. The response carries a WWW-Authenticate challenge.

Forbidden.description: The request origin was not permitted.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist. The code field distinguishes an unknown route from a valid resource with an unknown id.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but does not support this HTTP method.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state, such as an unsupported payload version.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request Content-Type is not accepted by this endpoint.

MisdirectedRequest.description: The request Host header was not a loopback address.

UnprocessableContent.description: The request was well-formed but semantically invalid and could not be applied, such as a document whose structure the product rejects. The code field identifies the specific problem.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The External Client API is disabled or shutting down.

Accepted.description: The command did not settle within the synchronous window. The body is the pending operation; poll the Location URL until it reaches a terminal state.

Location.description: Relative URL of the operation to poll.
